title: ADP Value and Reaching vs Falling (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: ADP Value (Reaching vs Falling). SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: The gap between a player's market average draft position and your own projected rank, signaling whether the field is over- or under-pricing him. INPUTS (general): player projections, public ADP, current draft slot. HOW TO READ IT: A player whose projected rank sits well ahead of his ADP is a value (let him fall); one taken far before his ADP is a reach. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to time picks and capture surplus instead of drafting strict best-player-available off a single ranking; beats taking your favorite name a full round early. COMMON MISTAKE: Reaching for a target you could have gotten a round later, burning the value the ADP gap was telling you to exploit. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Zero-RB Construction (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Zero-RB Construction. SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/PPR; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: A roster-build strategy that fades early running backs to load up on high-floor pass-catchers, then mines RB production from value and the waiver wire later. INPUTS (general): positional injury attrition, projected target volume, draft slot. HOW TO READ IT: Strong when WR/TE scoring is dense and RB injury risk is high; the build leans on contingent backs hitting in-season. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use in deeper PPR leagues to dodge fragile early-RB outcomes; beats reflexively spending the first three picks on running backs. COMMON MISTAKE: Going Zero-RB without a plan to acquire volume backs later, leaving a permanent hole at the position. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Robust-RB Construction (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Robust-RB Construction. SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: A build that front-loads multiple running backs early to corner a scarce, high-leverage position before it dries up. INPUTS (general): positional scarcity curve, projected RB workload, draft slot. HOW TO READ IT: Strong when the RB tier cliff is steep and waiver-wire RB replacement is unreliable. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use in standard or shallow leagues where startable RBs are scarce; beats spreading early picks thin across positions that replenish more easily. COMMON MISTAKE: Over-committing to RB in a year of deep RB supply, leaving the WR and TE corps weak. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Late-Round QB (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Late-Round QB. SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: A timing strategy that waits on quarterback because the weekly scoring gap between mid-tier and elite QBs is small relative to their draft cost. INPUTS (general): positional replacement level, projected QB scoring spread, draft slot. HOW TO READ IT: Strong in single-QB formats where streamable passers approximate elite output at a fraction of the price. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to spend premium capital on scarce RB/WR and grab QB late; beats reaching for a top QB in the early rounds in 1QB leagues. COMMON MISTAKE: Applying it in SuperFlex/2QB leagues, where QB scarcity flips and waiting becomes a trap. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Handcuff Value (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Handcuff Value. SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: The insurance value of drafting the direct backup to a starting running back, who inherits a featured workload if the starter is hurt. INPUTS (general): starter injury risk, backup's projected inherited role, depth-chart clarity. HOW TO READ IT: High when the backup would step into a clear lead role; low in committee backfields where the touches would scatter. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to protect a fragile early RB investment or speculate on standalone-plus-contingent upside; beats leaving a high-pick RB uninsured. COMMON MISTAKE: Handcuffing your own star too early instead of taking the highest-leverage backups across the league. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Contingent-Upside Lottery Backs (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Contingent-Upside (Lottery-Ticket Backs). SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: The conditional ceiling of a buried back whose value is near-zero in the base case but league-winning if a single event (injury, depth-chart shift) unlocks a featured role. INPUTS (general): path-to-touches probability, projected role if promoted, draft cost. HOW TO READ IT: Read it as an option value: low expected points but a fat right tail worth a late-round dart. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use late and in bulk to buy cheap exposure to high-variance outcomes; beats spending the same late picks on flat, capped veterans. COMMON MISTAKE: Pricing the lottery ticket like a starter and drafting it rounds too early. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Rookie Draft Capital Valuation (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Rookie Draft-Capital Valuation. SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: How a rookie's real-NFL draft slot predicts opportunity and fantasy outcome, since teams feed early-capital players touches and targets. INPUTS (general): NFL draft position, projected landing-spot role, positional age curve. HOW TO READ IT: High NFL draft capital signals an invested team and a likely path to volume; late capital signals a steeper climb. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to separate rookie hype from durable opportunity; beats ranking rookies on college stats or highlight reputation alone. COMMON MISTAKE: Ignoring landing spot, so a high-capital rookie stuck behind entrenched starters gets over-drafted. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Target-Share Projection (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Target-Share Projection. SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/PPR; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: A receiver's projected fraction of his team's total targets, the most stable upstream driver of PPR scoring. INPUTS (general): historical target share, projected role and depth-chart change, team pass volume. HOW TO READ IT: A high projected share signals dependable volume; a low share signals reliance on efficiency or touchdowns that regress. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to anchor WR/TE projections in repeatable usage; beats valuing pass-catchers off prior-year fantasy points, which bake in volatile efficiency. COMMON MISTAKE: Confusing raw catches with share, missing that a target share on a low-volume offense yields fewer looks. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Opportunity Share and Volume (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Opportunity Share (Total Volume). SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: A back's combined share of team carries plus targets, capturing total touch volume that drives fantasy floor more than per-touch efficiency. INPUTS (general): projected carry share, projected target share, team play volume. HOW TO READ IT: High opportunity share means a back accrues points on volume regardless of efficiency swings; low share means he needs big plays to score. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to find floor-stable RBs and to value pass-catching backs in PPR; beats ranking RBs on yards-per-carry, which is noisy and unstable year to year. COMMON MISTAKE: Crediting a strong rushing share while ignoring that a back ceded all third-down and goal-line work. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Air Yards and aDOT for Valuation (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Air Yards and aDOT. SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: The total downfield yardage a receiver is thrown and his average depth of target, capturing the size and shape of his receiving opportunity beyond catches. INPUTS (general): projected air-yards volume, average depth of target, target share. HOW TO READ IT: High air yards signal big-play and touchdown equity; a deep aDOT means a higher ceiling but a lower, spikier floor. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to spot receivers whose underlying opportunity outruns their box-score points; beats valuing WRs on receptions alone, which underrates field-stretchers. COMMON MISTAKE: Chasing raw air yards without weighing efficiency, drafting a deep threat whose volume never converts. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Red-Zone Opportunity (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Red-Zone Opportunity. SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: A player's share of his team's touches and targets inside the opponent's red zone, the high-leverage zone where touchdowns are scored. INPUTS (general): projected red-zone touch/target share, team red-zone trips, goal-line role. HOW TO READ IT: A high red-zone share signals durable touchdown equity; a low share warns that current scoring leans on long, unrepeatable plays. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to forecast touchdown floors and find goal-line specialists; beats projecting touchdowns off last year's total, which regresses hard. COMMON MISTAKE: Assuming a player keeps a goal-line role after a personnel change that hands those carries to someone else. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Touchdown Regression Candidates (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Touchdown Regression Candidates. SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: Players whose prior-year touchdown rate diverged from their underlying opportunity, flagging likely positive or negative regression in the coming year. INPUTS (general): prior touchdown total, expected touchdowns from opportunity, projected role continuity. HOW TO READ IT: Scoring above expected opportunity flags negative regression (a fade); scoring below flags positive regression (a buy). WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to find buy-low and sell-high targets at ADP; beats projecting next year off raw fantasy points that overweight fluky scoring. COMMON MISTAKE: Treating regression as guaranteed and ignoring that an elite role can sustain an above-expected rate. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Positional Age Curves (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Positional Age Curves. SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: The typical performance arc by position with age, since running backs peak and decline early while receivers and quarterbacks hold value longer. INPUTS (general): player age, positional aging shape, projected role. HOW TO READ IT: A back past his positional peak carries downside risk; an aging receiver or QB in a stable role retains value further out. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to discount older RBs and to avoid overpaying for cliff-risk; beats valuing players purely on last season without an aging prior. COMMON MISTAKE: Applying one aging curve to all positions, fading a 30-year-old WR as if he were a 30-year-old RB. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Landing Spot and Role Change (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Landing Spot (Role Change). SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: How a player's new team, scheme, and depth chart reshape his projected opportunity after a trade, signing, or coaching change. INPUTS (general): new-team target/touch competition, scheme tendencies, projected role. HOW TO READ IT: A clear path to volume in a high-pace pass-friendly offense raises value; crowded depth charts or run-heavy schemes suppress it. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to re-rank players who changed situations rather than carrying over last year's value; beats projecting from prior usage in a different system. COMMON MISTAKE: Anchoring to a player's old role and ignoring that opportunity is environment-dependent. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: QB-WR Stacking Value (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: QB-WR Stacking Value. SPORT: Fantasy Football (best-ball/tournament; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: The correlation benefit of rostering a quarterback together with his pass-catcher, so a big passing day scores twice on your team. INPUTS (general): intra-team scoring correlation, projected pass volume, format payout structure. HOW TO READ IT: High value in ceiling-seeking formats where correlated spikes win weeks; muted in points-only formats that reward stability. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use in best-ball and tournaments to raise team ceiling; beats picking the QB and WR independently as if their scores were unrelated. COMMON MISTAKE: Over-stacking in a redraft cash league where correlation adds variance without a payout for ceiling. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Bye-Week Stacking Avoidance (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Bye-Week Stacking Avoidance. SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: Roster concentration risk from drafting too many starters who share the same bye week, forcing a single crippled lineup week. INPUTS (general): players' bye weeks, starter concentration by position, roster depth. HOW TO READ IT: A cluster of key starters on one bye week is a red flag; spread byes signal a manageable schedule. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use as a late-round tiebreaker between similar players to smooth weekly lineups; beats ignoring byes and fielding a hollow team on a single week. COMMON MISTAKE: Letting bye-week avoidance override value, passing a clearly better player to dodge a manageable overlap. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Positional Run Dynamics (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Positional Run Dynamics (Tier Runs). SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: The cascade when several drafters take the same position in quick succession, draining a tier and shifting scarcity in real time. INPUTS (general): live positional supply by tier, opponents' roster needs, draft slot. HOW TO READ IT: An active run signals a tier is about to empty; reading it tells you whether to join the run or pivot to an untouched position. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to anticipate scarcity and grab the last player in a tier before the cliff; beats drafting in a vacuum off a static ranking. COMMON MISTAKE: Panic-joining a run and reaching for a lesser player when an untapped position offered better value. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Value-Based Drafting Variants (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Value-Based Drafting Variants. SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: The family of baselines used to convert projections into cross-position value, differing by how the replacement reference is defined (last-starter, worst-starter, or blended baselines). INPUTS (general): player projections, choice of replacement baseline, league starter requirements. HOW TO READ IT: Each baseline reshapes which position looks scarce; a steeper baseline pushes value toward thin positions. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to pick a baseline that matches your league's roster rules; beats comparing raw projected points across positions that play by different supply. COMMON MISTAKE: Adopting one baseline blindly and not realizing it systematically over- or under-rates a position for your settings. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Floor vs Ceiling Consistency (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Floor vs Ceiling (Consistency). SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: The week-to-week distribution of a player's outcomes, separating high-floor consistency from high-ceiling upside at the same projected average. INPUTS (general): projected mean, outcome variance, role stability. HOW TO READ IT: A high floor means dependable startable weeks; a high ceiling means spike potential with more bust risk. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use floor players to stabilize a strong roster and ceiling players to chase upside when behind; beats ranking on projected average alone, which hides distribution shape. COMMON MISTAKE: Filling every slot with low-ceiling floor players, building a team with no path to a blow-up week. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Strength of Schedule for Draft (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Strength of Schedule for Draft. SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: The aggregate difficulty of a player's upcoming matchups, especially weighted toward the fantasy playoff weeks, as a draft-day tiebreaker. INPUTS (general): opponent defensive strength by position, schedule timing, playoff-week matchups. HOW TO READ IT: A soft schedule, particularly late, is a modest tailwind; a brutal slate is a mild fade among comparable players. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use as a thin-margin tiebreaker and to weight playoff-week matchups; beats over-trusting full-season SOS when early projections of defenses are noisy. COMMON MISTAKE: Over-drafting on SOS, treating preseason defensive rankings as reliable when they shift through the year. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Dead-Zone RB Avoidance (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Dead-Zone RB. SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: A middle-round band of running backs whose ADP outpaces their expected production because they combine moderate cost with committee or injury-fragile roles. INPUTS (general): mid-round RB role ambiguity, ADP cost, opportunity-share projection. HOW TO READ IT: Backs in this band are priced like starters but profile like fliers; flagging the zone tells you where to fade. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to route mid-round capital to WRs or QBs and grab RB upside cheaper later; beats reflexively filling RB in the dead-zone band because the position feels thin. COMMON MISTAKE: Confusing a genuine value back with a dead-zone trap just because both sit in the same rounds. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Onesie Position Timing TE/QB (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Onesie Position Timing (TE/QB). SPORT: Fantasy Football (snake/points; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: When to draft single-roster-slot positions like tight end and quarterback, where a small elite tier creates a real edge but the rest are nearly interchangeable. INPUTS (general): positional scoring spread, size of the elite tier, draft slot. HOW TO READ IT: If the elite tier is small and far ahead, paying up early is justified; if the position is flat after the top names, wait. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to decide between an early elite onesie and a late streaming approach; beats treating TE and QB with the same timing every year regardless of tier shape. COMMON MISTAKE: Reaching for the fourth-best onesie, paying a premium for a player barely above replacement. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Best-Ball vs Managed Valuation (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Best-Ball vs Managed Valuation. SPORT: Fantasy Football (best-ball; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: How player value shifts when lineups auto-optimize with no in-season management, rewarding spike weeks and removing the cost of bye weeks and busts. INPUTS (general): outcome variance, spike-week frequency, roster depth needs. HOW TO READ IT: Ceiling and correlation gain value; consistency and bye-week planning lose importance versus managed redraft. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use to re-rank for best-ball by leaning into upside and stacks; beats importing managed-league rankings that overvalue floor and waiver-dependent players. COMMON MISTAKE: Drafting best-ball like redraft, fading high-variance ceiling players the format is built to reward. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Stars-and-Scrubs vs Balanced Budget (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Auction Budget Allocation (Stars-and-Scrubs vs Balanced). SPORT: Fantasy Football (auction; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: How to distribute a fixed auction budget, contrasting spending big on a few elite players and filling with minimums against spreading evenly for roster balance. INPUTS (general): total budget, positional value tiers, roster slots to fill. HOW TO READ IT: Stars-and-scrubs maximizes top-end talent but thins depth; a balanced spread buys reliability across the lineup. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use stars-and-scrubs when the elite tier is league-winning and waiver depth is strong; beats spending uniformly when a few players are clearly worth a premium. COMMON MISTAKE: Going stars-and-scrubs and running out of budget, fielding too many dollar-tier scrubs in starting slots. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).

title: Auction Nomination Strategy (Fantasy Football)
body: CONCEPT: Auction Nomination Strategy. SPORT: Fantasy Football (auction; draft-day). WHAT IT MEASURES: The tactical use of who you put up for bid to drain rivals' budgets, set price anchors, and steer the market toward players you want cheap. INPUTS (general): opponents' remaining budgets, positional scarcity state, your own targets. HOW TO READ IT: Nominating players you do not want forces rivals to spend; holding your targets until budgets thin lets you buy at a discount. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Use throughout the auction to manage the room's purchasing power; beats nominating your own targets early and inviting bidding wars. COMMON MISTAKE: Nominating a player you secretly want, then getting stuck overpaying when the bidding heats up. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Football (concept only).
